semantic_description: Functions in long-range contact and is an important component of the species' extended contact system.
acoustic_description: A clear narrowband element with longer duration than chirps and a smoother whistle-like contour.

semantic_description: Produced in threatening situations and can occur in sequences with other short call elements.
acoustic_description: A conspicuous abrupt call type harsher than the contact repertoire and suited for fast attention capture.

semantic_description: Used in capture, severe conflict, and other extreme disturbance.
acoustic_description: A high-arousal noisy call with strong amplitude and longer duration than brief alarm notes.

semantic_description: Reported as a composite signal used after alarm contexts, plausibly serving an all-clear or post-disturbance regrouping function.
acoustic_description: A compound sequence that combines an alarm-like element with a whistle-like contact element into a stereotyped multi-note phrase.

semantic_description: Produced during approach to preferred foods and during feeding, and can inform group members about food-related activity.
acoustic_description: A short chirp-class call used in food situations, with context-linked variants rather than a single invariant note shape.

semantic_description: Used in nearby social communication and likely overlaps functionally with other short contact-like signals.
acoustic_description: A brief trilled or rapidly modulated high-pitched call, intermediate in texture between a simple chirp and a longer whistle sequence.

semantic_description: Used in conspicuous disturbance, mobbing, or high-arousal alerting situations.
acoustic_description: A staccato bout of short abrupt notes with harsher structure than tonal chirps and whistles.

semantic_description: Produced when tamarins actively approach and harass a potential predator; recruits group members to participate in joint mobbing and may suppress predator attack.
acoustic_description: A harsh repetitive call produced in rapid bouts during active mobbing of a predator; acoustically distinct from single alarm notes in its sustained repetitive patterning and heightened intensity.

semantic_description: Produced by isolated infants and used to recruit maternal attention, retrieval, and recognition.
acoustic_description: A repeated high-pitched peep given in bouts, more persistent and attention-getting than routine low-arousal contact peeps.

semantic_description: Addressed by mothers or other caregivers to dependent infants before nursing, during nursing, or at nursing termination to coordinate reunion and infant handling.
acoustic_description: A brief low-frequency call, often harmonic and softer than alarm peeps or yaps, with subtle contextual variation across nursing phases.

semantic_description: Used in routine within-group social contact.
acoustic_description: A short local call with simple structure, often repeated in low-arousal interaction.

semantic_description: Used in local social communication and cohesion.
acoustic_description: A brief high-pitched tonal note with lighter structure than alarm calls.

semantic_description: Produced to alert nearby group members to dangerous or highly threatening situations.
acoustic_description: A peep-like call type with the same basic tonal shape as contact peeps but delivered more forcefully and in threat-related bouts.

semantic_description: Used in terrestrial-threat or mobbing-like alarm situations rather than the peep-based warning context.
acoustic_description: A harsher and less purely tonal alarm call than the alarm peep, typically delivered as repeated notes in conspicuous bouts.

semantic_description: Used in active social and movement contexts.
acoustic_description: A rapid sequence of high notes with more continuous repetition than a single peep.

semantic_description: Used in structured vocal exchanges, especially in close affiliative interactions and mother-infant contexts.
acoustic_description: A brief composite call with a rough introductory element followed by a chuck-like ending, acoustically more segmented than a simple chuck.

semantic_description: Reported especially from adult males during quarrels and other intense social disturbances.
acoustic_description: A loud, rough, rapidly repeated harsh call, more forceful and lower-pitched than peeps and more segmented than a sustained scream.

semantic_description: Used in socially tense or otherwise high-arousal disturbance contexts.
acoustic_description: A repeated bursty call series with rougher quality than peeps and more segmented structure than a scream.

semantic_description: Produced in danger, capture, or severe social conflict.
acoustic_description: A loud high-arousal call with noisy spectral structure and strong amplitude.

semantic_description: Produced during feeding, partial isolation, exploration, and greeting; functions in local cohesion and within-group coordination at close range.
acoustic_description: A brief, high-pitched tonal note with a slight upward or downward frequency sweep, structurally similar to a peep but typically faster and lighter in quality. Often produced in rapid sequences.

semantic_description: Produced specifically during social play interactions; rate increases with play intensity and is thought to signal motivation to continue play. May also have a metacommunicative function alerting nearby adults to ongoing play activity.
acoustic_description: A series of tonal peep-like notes produced during active play bouts; rate and complexity tend to increase with play bout duration; structurally related to other peep variants but contextually distinct.

semantic_description: Produced in contexts of self-confident or challenging social attitude; associated with affiliative or approach-related states rather than fear or submission. Controlled via the stria terminalis pathway.
acoustic_description: A soft, low-pitched, continuous or semi-continuous call with harmonic structure; short respiratory movements accompany the call; tonally smooth and low-amplitude.

semantic_description: Produced in mildly aversive or resentful social contexts; described as indicating flight motivation or resentment. Reported in positive social contexts (e.g., grooming) as well as mild disturbance.
acoustic_description: A low-pitched, somewhat noisy and drawn-out call with a rough tonal character, often with slight frequency modulation; acoustically intermediate between a tonal and a broadband call.

semantic_description: Produced in highly aversive situations including defensive threat contexts and extreme fear; elicited by brain stimulation of highly aversive neural substrates; distinct from the softer alarm peep.
acoustic_description: A loud, high-pitched, broadband call with strong energy across a wide frequency range; more intense and longer than a peep; typically produced as a single burst or short bout.

semantic_description: Produced in highly aversive social or predator-related situations; reported alongside shrieks and alarm peeps in the most threatening contexts; represents the most intense alarm or agitation vocalization category.
acoustic_description: A composite call combining shriek and cackle elements; loud, harsh, and repeated; acoustically more complex and segmented than a pure shriek; rapid bursting structure.

semantic_description: Used in close-range affiliative communication and within-group coordination; documented as one of the call types with distinct respiratory correlates and a recognized unit in the squirrel monkey vocal repertoire.
acoustic_description: A rapid, frequency-modulated series of brief tonal elements forming a rolled or trilled percept; faster repetition rate than twitter; notes are tightly spaced.

semantic_description: Used in agonistic contexts, including intragroup male rivalry and intergroup encounters; associated with high-arousal aggressive states.
acoustic_description: A low-pitched, rough, broadband vocalization with noisy spectral structure; lower and more sustained than a cackle or shriek; produced with relatively little harmonic patterning.

semantic_description: Produced in intraspecific mobbing contexts; expresses a self-confident, challenging attitude and an attempt to recruit fellow group members to mob a threat. Distinct from the cackle used in pure aggressive disturbance.
acoustic_description: A rapid series of sharp, noisy pulses; acoustically similar to a cackle but specifically associated with mobbing behaviour; higher rate and more mechanical than social cackles.

semantic_description: Produced by infants and juveniles in distress or high-arousal begging contexts; distinguished from scream by somewhat lower amplitude and the characteristic upward frequency sweep.
acoustic_description: A loud, high-pitched, noisy call with upward frequency sweep and strong amplitude; longer and more sustained than a peep; strong energy in upper frequencies.

semantic_description: Produced in close-contact non-aversive social situations; reported as a non-aversive contact call elicited from PAG stimulation sites; overlaps functionally with chuck but at lower arousal.
acoustic_description: A very brief, soft, low-frequency click-like tonal note; softer and more percussive than a chuck; sometimes produced as single notes rather than bouts.

semantic_description: Co-occurs with the genital display, a species-typical socio-sexual behaviour used in dominance assertion and communication of social status; produced spontaneously without external threat.
acoustic_description: A brief vocalization accompanying the stereotyped genital display; call structure is variable and graded; intermediate in acoustic character between social contact calls and arousal-related calls.

semantic_description: Produced by wild females during active foraging; caller identity and foraging activity are encoded in the call, enabling group members to locate productive foraging sites and maintain coordination during food-finding.
acoustic_description: A chuck-like call produced specifically during foraging and feeding bouts; field recordings of wild females showed structural variation correlated with foraging activity; shares the basic descending frequency contour of chucks but with distinctive temporal patterning.

semantic_description: Used in close social interactions, greeting and mutual approach; distinct from the twitter as a longer-range coordination call; part of the graded peep-twitter continuum in close-contact contexts.
acoustic_description: A short-range twitter delivered at lower amplitude than long-range contact calls; rapid note repetition but softer and less sustained than a full twitter bout; spectrographic syllables show tighter spacing than long-distance twitter.

semantic_description: Produced during copulation and immediately preceding or following mating; communicates sexual state to partner and possibly to surrounding group members.
acoustic_description: A brief repetitive tonal call produced during mating; related in structure to twitter or chuck variants but produced specifically in sexual context; call rate may increase with sexual arousal.

semantic_description: Used in routine social coordination and proximity maintenance.
acoustic_description: A short modulated contact call, often delivered in repeated series.

semantic_description: Used in ordinary social interaction and local communication.
acoustic_description: A rapid sequence of high notes with lighter tonal quality than barks.

semantic_description: Produced in disturbance and high-arousal alert contexts.
acoustic_description: A short harsh call with abrupt onset and broad spectral energy.

semantic_description: Common in aggressive encounters and victim responses.
acoustic_description: A loud high-arousal vocalization with noisy energy and strong contour variation.

semantic_description: Used in distance communication and cohesion; in tufted capuchins, whistle-series variants have also been linked to food and intergroup contexts.
acoustic_description: A clearer narrowband call with more sustained tonal structure than short trills or twitters.

semantic_description: Produced around food discovery or feeding competition and can affect nearby individuals.
acoustic_description: A repeated short tonal call type used in food situations, structurally closer to local contact calls than to barks.

semantic_description: A broadly conserved capuchin low-level threat used in mild aggressive or displacement contexts.
acoustic_description: A brief slightly atonal squeaky threat note, typically given singly rather than in long bouts.

semantic_description: Likely used to regain contact with separated group members, consistent with other capuchins and later Sapajus repertoire work.
acoustic_description: A louder, lower-frequency distance call given in short bouts and more far-carrying than routine contact trills.

semantic_description: The most frequently produced call in the repertoire, used to regulate within-group spacing and maintain cohesion during movement and foraging.
acoustic_description: A brief soft tonal note, often given singly or in loose sequences; structurally simple with relatively stable fundamental frequency and short duration.

semantic_description: Produced exclusively by infants in social and proximity-maintenance contexts; may escalate in distress situations when separated from the mother.
acoustic_description: Rapid sequences of short high-pitched tonal notes with variable frequency modulation; structurally more variable and less stereotyped than adult contact notes.

semantic_description: A distinctive contact call used in longer-range within-group communication; categorized as a separate contact call type in Sapajus libidinosus repertoire studies and likely present in S. apella.
acoustic_description: A sustained tonal call with prominent frequency sweep, rising or rising-falling contour, and harmonic structure; more complex and longer-duration than the contact note.

semantic_description: Produced by animals actively foraging or feeding; serves to maintain group coordination during food search and may signal food-patch presence to nearby group members.
acoustic_description: A class of soft repeated tonal calls produced during foraging; the chihui is a contact note followed by one to three higher-pitched notes, while the grgr is a more rapid short series; structurally intermediate between a contact note and a food call.

semantic_description: Produced in moderate-to-high-intensity aggressive interactions; used in direct threats toward conspecifics and agonistic displays; distinct from the brief mild-threat heh call.
acoustic_description: A series of rapid abrupt pulsed notes with rising frequency or intensity; can range from short cough-like units (cough-cough) to rapid pip sequences and full ascending staccato bouts.

semantic_description: Produced specifically in response to aerial predators (raptors) and sometimes humans; distinct from barks given to terrestrial threats; elicits upward scanning and flight-to-cover responses in listeners.
acoustic_description: A short high-pitched tonal or semi-tonal call acoustically distinct from the terrestrial alarm bark; tends to be higher in frequency and sharper in onset than ground-predator barks.

semantic_description: Produced in reproductive contexts including mate attraction, copulation, and sexual displays; linked to solicitation and assessment of reproductive state.
acoustic_description: A low, somewhat raspy short vocalization; in males described as a chuck with noisy broadband quality; females may produce a raspier version during oestrus or copulation; graded in intensity.

semantic_description: Main adult male advertisement used in mate attraction and territory-related display, especially during the breeding season.
acoustic_description: Rich, flowing warbling song composed of repeated syllables, trills, whistles, and rapid frequency-modulated note sequences that can be assembled into longer bouts.

semantic_description: Used in routine flocking, perching, and local social coordination between nearby individuals.
acoustic_description: Short, light, twittering notes or brief call strings, simpler and shorter than full song.

semantic_description: Helps maintain cohesion and coordinate movement when birds depart, pass overhead, or shift positions within flocks.
acoustic_description: Brief, simple notes delivered in flight or at takeoff, generally more clipped than the contact twitter.

semantic_description: Given in disturbance or predator contexts and treated here as a broad alarm class documented in field recording archives.
acoustic_description: Sharp, clipped single notes or short note strings that are more abrupt and tense than the routine twitter contact call.

semantic_description: Produced by females in response to male song quality and during sexual signalling in breeding contexts.
acoustic_description: Short vocal signals given by females in reproductive contexts, typically much simpler than male song.

semantic_description: Used by young birds to obtain provisioning and parental attention.
acoustic_description: A repeated solicitation call produced by nestlings or fledglings.

semantic_description: Produced by juvenile males during sensorimotor vocal learning; represents practice vocalisation prior to crystallisation of adult song.
acoustic_description: Soft, poorly structured, variable vocalization with loosely organised syllables and frequent hesitations; louder and more stereotyped plastic-song phase follows before crystallisation into adult song.

semantic_description: Given during close-range aggressive encounters such as competition for perch sites, food resources, or territory boundaries; overlapping song by a rival male can also function as an aggressive signal.
acoustic_description: Short, harsh or raspy notes that are acoustically distinct from the tonal contact twitter; more broadband and abrupt in structure.

semantic_description: Produced when a bird is handled, restrained, or under acute stress; may alert conspecifics to immediate danger or physical distress.
acoustic_description: Loud, urgent, high-pitched notes repeated at rapid rate; distinct from the quieter routine contact twitter.

semantic_description: Used in sexual and territorial display, especially by breeding adults at colony sites.
acoustic_description: A prolonged display sequence combining repeated syllables into a conspicuous rhythmic bout.

semantic_description: Used for partner or colony contact and long-range social advertisement.
acoustic_description: A far-carrying, donkey-like vocalization with strong harmonic structure and repeated syllabic pattern.

semantic_description: Used in close-range pair, parent-offspring, and neighbor interactions.
acoustic_description: A shorter, softer call than the main display signals, with simple harmonic structure.

semantic_description: Produced in nest defense, agonistic encounters, or close-range colony disputes.
acoustic_description: A sharp, harsh call with abrupt delivery and a noisier structure than contact calls.

semantic_description: Produced by chicks or juveniles to solicit feeding and parental attention.
acoustic_description: A repeated juvenile solicitation call thinner and more urgent than adult contact or display calls.

semantic_description: Used in close-range partner or parent-young recognition and local cohesion.
acoustic_description: A softer repeated contact call with more regular tonal structure than the louder bray call.

semantic_description: Often used in male display and territorial contexts and serves as a prominent advertisement signal.
acoustic_description: A short, clear, stereotyped whistle-rich song with strong tonal structure and relatively discrete phrase boundaries.

semantic_description: Used mainly in sexual display and prolonged social advertisement, especially toward females.
acoustic_description: A longer, more variable, jumbled song containing whistles, warbles, rattles, trills, and imitated sounds.

semantic_description: Used during routine social interactions and flock-level coordination.
acoustic_description: A local social sequence of short harsher notes with less formal phrase structure than song.

semantic_description: Included as a conspicuous component of starling vocal output in aroused display or close social interaction.
acoustic_description: A rapid harsh series with strong noisy energy and mechanical or rattling quality.

semantic_description: A learned display-rich component of starling song that may contribute to sexual and social signaling.
acoustic_description: A vocal sequence containing copied heterospecific or environmental sounds embedded within normal starling song structure.

semantic_description: Used to maintain contact and coordinate movement in flocks.
acoustic_description: A short simple call given during takeoff and flight, less variable than the warbling song types.

semantic_description: Produced in response to predators or sudden disturbance; causes conspecifics to take flight or freeze.
acoustic_description: A harsher abrupt call distinct from song and rattle sequences, typically broadband with steep onset.

semantic_description: Given when a bird is seized or attacked by a predator; may function to startle the predator and alert nearby conspecifics.
acoustic_description: A high-pitched, harsh, penetrating scream with wide frequency modulation and irregular rapid note sequences; acoustically distinct from the aggression screams.

semantic_description: Produced during direct physical encounters with conspecifics, typically accompanied by wing-flapping and bill gaping.
acoustic_description: A harsh chattering scream often transcribed as "chackerchackerchacker"; rapid repetition of noisy, broadband pulses.

semantic_description: Used during intraspecific encounters to threaten rivals at close range, often accompanied by wing-waving; distinct from the full attack call.
acoustic_description: A high-pitched trill or scream used at close range during agonistic encounters; shorter and more tonal than the attack call.

semantic_description: Given repeatedly when mobbing avian predators, when alighting into an established group, or at roost entries; recruits conspecifics to mob a predator.
acoustic_description: A sharp metallic chip note, repeated persistently; higher-pitched and more discrete than the alarm call.

semantic_description: Produced by females during copulation; exact function unclear but likely signals receptivity or pair-bonding context.
acoustic_description: A brief, relatively quiet call of moderate pitch emitted by the female during or immediately following copulation; poorly characterized acoustically in the literature.

semantic_description: Produced by nestlings and recently fledged juveniles to solicit food from parents; intensity increases with hunger level.
acoustic_description: Persistent, high-pitched, broad-bandwidth calls with noisy texture; minimum frequency shifts upward in response to background noise. Juveniles produce a more drawn-out version of this call.

semantic_description: A motor-rehearsal phase of vocal learning in young males starting around 3 months of age; not directed at specific receivers; precedes crystallization of the adult warbling song and whistled song.
acoustic_description: A low-amplitude, highly variable and disorganized vocalization resembling a murmured version of adult warbling song; basic note groupings into motifs are present from the start but structure is initially very variable, crystallizing gradually over several months.

semantic_description: Produced by starlings assembling at staging areas before roosting; thought to facilitate coordination of when and where to enter the roost.
acoustic_description: A mix of chatter and short calls produced by individuals in pre-roost aggregations; collectively creates a persistent roar or hum from the flock. Individual-level calls are similar to flock contact and chatter notes.

semantic_description: Frequently given when a bird takes flight or is handled; also used as a close-range contact signal among flock members.
acoustic_description: A soft rolling purring note, sometimes transcribed as "prurrp"; lower-pitched and softer than the flight call.

semantic_description: Given to flying or overhead predators and elicits rapid vigilance and refuge-seeking responses from group members.
acoustic_description: A brief alarm call with abrupt onset and relatively harsh spectral structure, often emitted in rapid sequences under high threat.

semantic_description: Produced when a ground-based predator or comparable terrestrial threat is detected, allowing listeners to adjust their escape and scanning behavior.
acoustic_description: A short alarm call that is typically more harmonic and less harsh at lower urgency, but can become noisier and more abrupt as urgency increases.

semantic_description: Used when group members are recruited to inspect, mob, or collectively respond to a threat such as a snake or other target requiring coordinated attention.
acoustic_description: A repeated, high-arousal alarm series with harsh elements that stands out strongly from low-risk calls.

semantic_description: Maintains contact and spacing among foraging group members and helps coordinate group cohesion under low perceived risk.
acoustic_description: A soft, low-amplitude call given frequently during foraging, with simple short tonal structure.

semantic_description: Produced by guarding individuals to signal ongoing vigilance and modulate the perceived safety of foraging group mates.
acoustic_description: A repeated sequence of low-amplitude tonal calls that can vary subtly with changes in perceived safety and vigilance state.

semantic_description: Associated with coordinated group movement and helps keep individuals together while shifting position between patches or burrows.
acoustic_description: A short, repeated call type used in locomotor contexts, acoustically similar to other low-arousal social calls but typically given in movement bouts.

semantic_description: Elicits food transfer or attention from helpers and breeders during juvenile provisioning and post-emergence care.
acoustic_description: A repeated, high-pitched call often delivered persistently by dependent young during provisioning interactions.

semantic_description: Produced under immediate high-risk threat and associated with the fastest escape responses.
acoustic_description: A very urgent alarm call with harsh abrupt structure and higher amplitude than routine aerial or terrestrial alarms.

semantic_description: Produced by group members after emerging from sleeping burrows during communal sunning, with a likely social regulatory and bonding function. Call rate is influenced by social relationships and dominance status.
acoustic_description: A soft, brief, tonal call produced mainly in morning sunning bouts; approximately 50-55 dB at half a metre. Individuals avoid overlapping one another, resulting in a turn-taking rhythm within the group.

semantic_description: Produced by subordinates during social tension with same-sex dominants, typically combined with submissive body posture and often followed by grooming or following behaviour. Among the most frequently produced call types in the meerkat repertoire.
acoustic_description: Rapid, high-pitched, brief tonal notes produced in bouts by subordinate individuals. Bout structure follows Menzerath's Law (longer sequences have shorter elements). Bouts may incorporate single-note, double-note, triple-note, and multiple-note variants.

semantic_description: Produced during aggressive intragroup or intergroup encounters. Low growls and snarls are used in dominance interactions, while louder barks are directed at rival groups encroaching on territory boundaries.
acoustic_description: Harsh, low-pitched broadband vocalisations including growls and louder barks with abrupt onset. Acoustically distinct from the high-pitched tonal alarm and contact calls.

semantic_description: Produced by individuals that become separated from the group, facilitating reunion. Also reported in pups that lose contact with group members above ground.
acoustic_description: A repeated, relatively loud tonal call with rising contour produced by isolated or separated individuals. Higher amplitude and more persistent than foraging contact calls.

semantic_description: Produced mainly by pair-bonded adults as a coordinated display for pair cohesion and advertisement of occupancy to neighboring groups.
acoustic_description: A prolonged high-amplitude song bout built from repeated phrases and coordinated contributions by pair members, often combining low booming elements with louder ringing screams and bark-like notes.

semantic_description: Characteristic adult male contribution to long-range song displays, especially during duet performance and advertisement toward other groups.
acoustic_description: Deep resonant low-frequency pulses produced in repeated series, carrying farther than most higher-pitched elements.

semantic_description: Used as a conspicuous display element within the adult song repertoire and in aroused situations requiring attention at longer range.
acoustic_description: Loud bark-like notes with abrupt onset and broad spectral energy, standing out clearly from the more tonal song elements.

semantic_description: Prominent adult female display signal in pair song, contributing to coordinated territorial advertisement and pair-level performance.
acoustic_description: High-pitched far-carrying screams with strong modulation and a wavering or ululating quality, often among the most salient elements of the bout.

semantic_description: Treated here as a distinctive female display element within song bouts; likely important for caller or pair distinctiveness even if exact functional separation from other screams is uncertain.
acoustic_description: A loud scream with two simultaneous tonal bands or a strongly dual-structured frequency pattern, giving it a bitonal quality.

semantic_description: Used in local arousal or disturbance contexts when a full duet sequence is not produced.
acoustic_description: A short harsh bark produced outside the sustained rhythmic structure of a full bout.

semantic_description: Produced as a distinct note type within song bouts and territorial displays; pairs can produce either boom or wow notes in alternation or combination, contributing to the variety of the song phrase structure.
acoustic_description: A resonant, higher-pitched note produced with the mouth open and throat sac inflated, contrasting with the closed-mouth deep boom; carries less far than the boom but is still loud and carries clear tonal structure.

semantic_description: Close-range contact vocalization used between group members during foraging, travel, and other non-song social contexts; analogous to the well-described hoo calls of other hylobatids; exact siamang-specific contexts await detailed study.
acoustic_description: Soft, short, low-amplitude tonal note at relatively low frequency; acoustically inconspicuous compared to song elements; typically a single brief syllable.

semantic_description: Produced by infants and juveniles during separation from caregivers, handling, or distress; functions to elicit parental approach and caregiving responses.
acoustic_description: High-pitched, often noisy scream or squeal with rapid frequency modulation; may be prolonged in series when distress is acute; higher in pitch and less structured than adult song screams.

semantic_description: Produced mainly by males in courtship and display contexts and carries individual information.
acoustic_description: A learned courtship song composed of a repeated sequence of syllables with stable phrase structure and rich spectro-temporal variation.

semantic_description: Used to maintain pair or flock contact when separated and can encode individual or social information.
acoustic_description: A louder contact call than routine social notes, typically tonal and modulated, suited for communication over greater distance.

semantic_description: Used in ordinary close-range flock or pair communication.
acoustic_description: A brief simple call, typically shorter and less intense than distance calls.

semantic_description: Used in close social interactions within pair or group settings.
acoustic_description: A compact short call type differing from tet and distance calls in contour and social deployment.

semantic_description: Used to elicit provisioning and parental attention from adults.
acoustic_description: A repeated solicitation call given by dependent young, simpler than adult song and contact calls.

semantic_description: Used in local pair coordination around the nest and during close social interaction.
acoustic_description: A soft close-range call associated with pair or nest interactions and lower amplitude than distance calls.

semantic_description: Produced during early pair bonding, around nesting activities, and sometimes in copulation contexts, often as part of close-range duets near the nest.
acoustic_description: A soft harmonic call with a slowly modulated pitch, relatively long duration, and low-frequency spectral emphasis that gives it a distinctly whining quality.

semantic_description: Used in aggressive supplanting and short-range conflict, especially near nests during nest-building or brooding.
acoustic_description: A brief very noisy hiss-like call with broad bandwidth and unusually low-frequency formants compared with the harmonic contact calls.

semantic_description: Produced when birds are physically restrained, isolated in aversive conditions, or experience acute stress; functions to attract conspecific attention and potentially elicit rescue behavior.
acoustic_description: A loud, long harmonic call with marked frequency modulation and high amplitude; typically more intense and sustained than contact calls, sometimes with a series of components that rise and fall in pitch.

semantic_description: Produced by chicks and juveniles as a precursor to the adult distance call; used for long-range contact with parents or flock members before adult call structure is fully crystallized.
acoustic_description: A long, tonal, harmonically rich call with gradual frequency modulation; structurally simpler than adult distance calls but serving a similar contact function in chicks.

semantic_description: Used in routine close-range social contact and as a common element in affiliative exchanges.
acoustic_description: A brief low-pitched grunt produced on exhalation, with a simple tonal to mildly noisy structure.

semantic_description: Used in low-arousal social contact and often incorporated into longer affiliative vocal sequences.
acoustic_description: A longer smooth low-frequency call with clear harmonic structure and sustained energy.

semantic_description: Typically appears inside elaborate social sequences rather than as a dominant standalone long-range call.
acoustic_description: A short inspiratory grunt with clipped structure and a distinct inhaled sound quality.

semantic_description: Used as part of socially rich affiliative sequences, especially in leader-male interactions with females.
acoustic_description: A sustained inhaled call with tonal harmonic energy and more drawn-out contour than inhale grunts.

semantic_description: A characteristic component of elaborate affiliative display sequences, especially in male-female interactions.
acoustic_description: A rhythmically modulated call with rapid pitch variation and a more elaborate harmonic pattern than simple moans or grunts.

semantic_description: Often occurs in elaborate social sequences and conspicuous social displays, particularly by leader males.
acoustic_description: A long conspicuous call with wide mouth opening, broad dynamic change, and a more expansive structure than moans or wobbles.

semantic_description: Produced immediately before mating during sexual interactions.
acoustic_description: A brief repeated sexual call with a relatively high-pitched, aroused structure.

semantic_description: Emitted at the termination of copulation.
acoustic_description: A short call given at the end of copulation, typically more clipped than longer affiliative sequence elements.

semantic_description: Produced during copulation by males and sometimes by females as part of the mating interaction itself.
acoustic_description: A variable-length sequence of repeated copulatory notes, usually given in rapid succession and more rhythmically repetitive than ordinary contact grunts.

semantic_description: Given after copulation and used to prolong or smooth the affiliative interaction between partners after genital contact ends.
acoustic_description: A post-mating vocal sequence assembled from softer affiliative close-call elements rather than a single stereotyped note.

semantic_description: Produced in conflict, harassment, and acute social tension.
acoustic_description: Loud harsh calls with strong noisy energy and marked arousal.

semantic_description: Given in predator detection or sudden danger, functioning as an alert to nearby group members.
acoustic_description: A short harsh exhaled bark with broad noisy energy and little tonal structure.

semantic_description: Produced by subordinate individuals toward higher-ranking animals in fearful or appeasing situations.
acoustic_description: A cough-like exhaled bark, typically brief and harsh, often with retracted lips.

semantic_description: Used by dominant or assertive individuals during aggressive encounters and close-range intimidation.
acoustic_description: A clipped staccato exhaled grunt that is acoustically harsher and more abrupt than routine affiliative grunts.

semantic_description: Produced especially by non-leader or bachelor males during competitive chases and other high-arousal male-male confrontations.
acoustic_description: A high-pitched bark-whinny type call, louder and more elongated than a simple bark and often given in repeated bursts.

semantic_description: Produced mainly by leader males during ritualized chase displays with rival males, where it advertises quality and competitive ability.
acoustic_description: A conspicuous two-part loud call with a distinct two-syllable structure given in bouts of repeated calls during display events.

semantic_description: Produced by bachelor or follower males during competitive confrontations with harem-holding leader males; associated with branch-shaking and tree-climbing threat displays.
acoustic_description: A forceful call combining a sustained low roar component followed by or merged with a sharp bark element, loud and broadband with strong noisy energy.

semantic_description: Emitted by leader males while herding females and in competitive interactions; used to direct female movement and reinforce dominance.
acoustic_description: A high-pitched, sharply produced squeal with tonal character, brief and piercing.

semantic_description: Appears within male affiliative vocal sequences directed at females; documented as a distinct derived call type though often produced overlapping with other vocalizations.
acoustic_description: A short inspiratory grunt with a distinctly nasal resonance quality, acoustically separable from the oral inhale grunt by its nasal formant coloration.

semantic_description: Produced during close affiliative interactions; the voiced variant of the motor-vocal lip-smack that is the phylogenetic precursor of the more elaborate derived wobble calls.
acoustic_description: A rhythmically pulsed vocalization produced during lip-smacking at 3–8 Hz, with voiced components superimposed on the orofacial rhythm; shares spectro-temporal patterning with human speech rhythm.

semantic_description: Produced in low-arousal close-contact situations and during appeasement interactions; part of the graded continuum of low-frequency affiliative calls.
acoustic_description: A low drawn-out call with a deep pitch and sustained harmonic structure, acoustically intermediate between a grunt and a moan but with a heavier, more resonant timbre.

semantic_description: Emitted during foraging and travelling bouts; females' contact grunts differ acoustically across foraging, travelling, and social states, and travel-state grunts serve spatial cohesion at the band level.
acoustic_description: A soft short grunt acoustically similar to close-contact exhale grunts but produced at higher rates during group movement; individual acoustic structure shifts slightly with behavioral state.

semantic_description: Produced by female victims during or immediately after agonistic attacks; recognized by other group members and by males who may respond with affiliative vocalizations as appeasement.
acoustic_description: A loud, sustained, broadly noisy scream with high fundamental frequency and significant energy across a wide frequency band, distinct from the shorter and harsher fear bark.

semantic_description: The scream-grunt series is the typical sequence following an agonistic interaction: a distress scream followed by a comforting grunt, which signals de-escalation. Sequences can also be reversed (grunt then scream) in ambivalent contexts.
acoustic_description: A compound vocal unit pairing an initial scream element (noisy, high-frequency, high arousal) with one or more following grunt elements (lower-frequency, tonal, lower arousal) within a rapid temporal window.

semantic_description: Produced predominantly by high-ranking males during periods of elevated social tension; has a strong auditory component and is associated with scratching and anxiety signals; contagious through auditory channel.
acoustic_description: A vocalized yawn produced with wide gape and head movement, encompassing a large frequency bandwidth and often with audible noisy components; acoustically distinct from low-intensity social and non-social yawn vocalizations.

semantic_description: Produced toward dominants or former aggressors in post-conflict contexts; functions as a reassurance or appeasement signal to reduce tension and facilitate reconciliation after agonistic interactions.
acoustic_description: A soft, muted exhale grunt delivered in close proximity; lower amplitude and more subdued quality than routine affiliative contact grunts, sometimes structurally transitional between a grunt and a groan.

semantic_description: Produced in low-arousal social contexts; shows a distinct acoustic profile from both high-intensity social yawns and non-social yawns; triggers yawn contagion via auditory channel in bystanders.
acoustic_description: A vocalized yawn with uncovered teeth but without the head movement and loud acoustic profile of the high-intensity variant; intermediate bandwidth and lower amplitude than YW3.

semantic_description: Given by group members in response to a close, low-urgency threat or predator detection. Functions to direct group attention to a potential danger without triggering full group flight. Also combined with the recruitment call into a mobbing sequence when terrestrial predators are encountered.
acoustic_description: A short, sharp, tonal note produced at close range. Typically a brief, high-pitched unit delivered singly or in quick succession. Acoustically distinct from the recruitment call, differing in note structure and repetition pattern.

semantic_description: Used when recruiting group members during locomotion and group movement between foraging areas. When combined with the alert call into a mobbing sequence upon encountering terrestrial predators, it apparently signals both the nature of the threat and the requested action (approach/mob).
acoustic_description: A structurally distinct call from the alert call, often frequency-modulated with a characteristic contour. Delivered in series during group locomotion or to coordinate movement. Can be distinguished from the alert call by its temporal patterning and acoustic shape.

semantic_description: Produced specifically upon encountering a terrestrial predator. Functions compositionally: the alert component communicates threat information while the recruitment component solicits approach and mobbing by other group members. Elicits stronger group response and faster approach than either component alone.
acoustic_description: A compound vocalization formed by combining the alert call and the recruitment call in sequence. The sequence is acoustically distinguishable from either component call alone and from control sequences, and listeners show stronger behavioural responses to it than to individual component calls.

semantic_description: Produced by adults when drawing young offspring (nestlings and fledglings) to a food source. Functions as a teaching signal: fledglings learn to associate the purr with food and to approach and follow adults when they hear it. Also used post-fledging to encourage movement across the territory toward foraging patches.
acoustic_description: A sustained, repetitive, low-to-mid frequency purring vocalization composed of approximately 17 repeated elements on average. Longer and more extended than the cluck call. The high element-repetition rate distinguishes it from the cluck (2–3 elements) with which it shares the same basic sound type.

semantic_description: Functions to collectively signal an imminent change in foraging site, coordinating group-level movement between patches. Not directed at offspring specifically; used in adult-to-adult coordination during foraging bouts.
acoustic_description: A truncated version of the purr, composed of 2–3 repeated elements of the same basic sound type as the purr. Acoustically compact and brief. The low element count distinguishes it from the full purr.

semantic_description: Produced by the designated sentinel during guard bouts, informing foraging group members of the sentinel's presence, position, and the current level of risk. Foragers increase use of exposed patches and reduce personal vigilance in response to this call, increasing foraging efficiency. Absence of the call signals elevated risk.
acoustic_description: A continuous, repetitive series of calls produced at a steady rate by an individual acting as sentinel from an elevated perch. Delivered persistently throughout a sentinel bout, providing a continuous acoustic signal of the sentry's presence and vigilance state to foragers below.

semantic_description: Produced by sentinels as they conclude guard bouts. May function to coordinate the handover of sentinel duties, minimizing time the group is without an active sentinel. Alternatively may signal changes in current risk level, modulating when the next sentinel bout begins.
acoustic_description: Short, rapid chuck notes produced at a fast rate. Acoustically compact and staccato. Distinct from the slower, sustained watchman's song produced during active sentinel bouts. Given in bursts at the end of a sentinel guard session.

semantic_description: Functions to regulate inter-individual spacing among foraging group members, reducing competition for prey. Group members maintain spacing and minimize aggressive encounters by responding to close calls from nearby conspecifics. Among the most frequently heard vocalizations during foraging bouts.
acoustic_description: Short, low-amplitude calls produced frequently during foraging at close range between group members. Soft and relatively inconspicuous, typical of short-range contact calls in social species.

semantic_description: Produced during intergroup encounters and territorial border disputes. Strongly territorial species engage in near-daily border defense, and chorusing is a key component of this territorial display. Also functions to reinforce group cohesion and signal group size/identity to rival groups.
acoustic_description: High-intensity, multi-individual babbling vocalization produced collectively by the group. Noisy, broadband and overlapping, creating a loud chorus. Individual variation exists in contribution to chorus. Classified into distinct subtypes (v-shaped chatter, double note ascending chatter, atonal chatter) that may serve different functions.

semantic_description: Produced by nestlings at the nest and by fledglings following adult group members during post-fledging dependence. Solicits food from parents and alloparents. Begging intensity and rate may be modulated by hunger level. Fledglings begging during second broods risk parental aggression.
acoustic_description: Persistent, high-pitched, repetitive calls produced by nestlings and fledglings when soliciting food from provisioning adults. Noisy and broadband with a somewhat grating quality. Repeated frequently while following adults.

semantic_description: Produced when aerial predators (raptors, hawks) are detected. Fork-tailed drongos exploit pied babbler alarm calls by mimicking them to steal food; both aerial and terrestrial alarm calls elicit flight-to-cover responses in pied babblers. Evidence from drongo mimicry studies confirms pied babblers produce distinct aerial alarm responses.
acoustic_description: A high-pitched, tonal, short alarm call produced in response to aerial predators such as raptors. Likely high-frequency and structurally distinct from terrestrial alarm calls, consistent with convergent evolution of aerial alarm call structure across bird species (thin, hard-to-localize).

semantic_description: Given in response to terrestrial predators such as snakes and mammalian carnivores. Unlike the aerial alarm, tends to elicit approach and mobbing behavior rather than flight to cover, especially when combined with the recruitment call. Drongos also mimic terrestrial alarm calls to steal food from foraging babblers.
acoustic_description: A broadband, noisy short alarm vocalization acoustically distinct from the aerial alarm call. Likely harsher and more broadband than aerial alarms, consistent with functional differentiation seen in related babblers (Turdoides squamiceps) where different predator classes elicit structurally different alarm vocalizations.

semantic_description: Produced in intragroup dominance interactions and boundary disputes. Used by dominant individuals to assert priority and repel rivals or subordinates in competition for food or breeding positions. Also used during intergroup encounters at territorial boundaries.
acoustic_description: A harsh, broadband, relatively loud call produced during agonistic interactions. May be graded in intensity proportional to the level of social threat. Distinct from alarm calls by its interactional context and lower pitch profile.

semantic_description: Produced by subordinate individuals to signal low-threat intent or to de-escalate agonistic interactions with dominant group members. Pied babblers have a well-described dominance hierarchy within groups, and subordinates engage in vocal appeasement behaviors to maintain their position and access to shared resources.
acoustic_description: Soft, tonal, quiet calls produced by subordinate individuals during or after agonistic encounters with dominant group members. Low amplitude and non-threatening acoustic profile.

semantic_description: Used for individual identification, contact, and reunion among group members.
acoustic_description: A narrowband modulated whistle with a characteristic individually distinctive contour.

semantic_description: Used in general social communication and coordination beyond individual signature signalling.
acoustic_description: A tonal whistle lacking the stereotyped individually distinctive contour of signature whistles, often more variable in shape.

semantic_description: Often associated with aroused social interactions and close-range confrontation.
acoustic_description: A rapidly pulsed broadband sound distinct from tonal whistles, often appearing harsh or compressed.

semantic_description: Often associated with foraging and coordinated social behaviour, especially in populations where bray sequences are common.
acoustic_description: A rhythmic multi-unit sequence built from repeated pulsed elements such as gulps, grunts, or squeaks in stereotyped order.

semantic_description: Primarily used in biosonar but socially informative during foraging and movement.
acoustic_description: A train of brief broadband clicks lacking sustained tonality.

semantic_description: Used at close range during prey pursuit and capture.
acoustic_description: A very rapid click sequence with greatly shortened inter-click intervals compared with ordinary echolocation trains.

semantic_description: Closely associated with successful prey capture and post-capture arousal.
acoustic_description: A high-pitched squeal-like burst or mixed signal given immediately after prey capture, often with a variable rough or pulsed quality.

semantic_description: Included as a named broad call class because gulps are repeatedly described as constituent units of bottlenose dolphin bray-call sequences.
acoustic_description: A brief pulsed element with a compact, percussive quality, often appearing as one component within longer bray-like sequences.

semantic_description: Included because grunt-like elements are regularly distinguished in bottlenose call reviews and in descriptions of bray-call sequences.
acoustic_description: A short low-frequency pulsed sound with rougher structure than a whistle and less sequence-level organization than a full bray call.

semantic_description: Included as a recurring named element in bottlenose bray-call and repertoire descriptions rather than collapsing it fully into whistle or burst-pulsed categories.
acoustic_description: A short high-pitched harsh signal, typically briefer and less contour-rich than a whistle and often embedded in multi-element sequences.

semantic_description: Used especially in response to aerial predators and other threats best handled by immediate vigilance or retreat.
acoustic_description: A sustained tonal alarm call with clear narrow-band structure and relatively long duration.

semantic_description: Often associated with terrestrial predators or close high-risk situations.
acoustic_description: A rapid series of alarm notes, longer as a bout than a single whistle and acoustically associated with repeated elements.

semantic_description: Used for lower-urgency terrestrial disturbance, humans, or lingering vigilance after a predator has been detected.
acoustic_description: A short narrow-band alarm note, less extended than whistles and less repetitive than trill bouts.

semantic_description: Produced in capture or acute danger situations.
acoustic_description: A harsh high-pitched call with abrupt onset and strong distress quality.

semantic_description: Produced by males immediately following copulation, possibly advertising dominance status or mating success to conspecifics.
acoustic_description: A multiple-note trill acoustically distinct from anti-predator trills; individually distinctive in structure, allowing individual recognition.

semantic_description: Produced during agonistic encounters between conspecifics; less stereotyped than alarm or mating trills.
acoustic_description: Multiple-note trill produced during social conflict; acoustically more variable than both anti-predator and post-copulatory trills, suggesting a graded or context-variable signal.

semantic_description: Produced by young juveniles, eliciting maternal attention; ceases at approximately 3-4 weeks after above-ground emergence as young become independent.
acoustic_description: Short, high-pitched tonal calls produced by young before or shortly after emergence above ground.

semantic_description: Used in long-range advertisement, intergroup spacing, and high-arousal social coordination; it is the species' best-known conspicuous display call.
acoustic_description: A conspicuous long-distance chorus composed of harsh roaring and shrieking elements from one or several callers, often with repeated phrases and very high amplitude.

semantic_description: Produced in long-distance advertisement and aroused social situations, either singly or as a component of larger chorus bouts.
acoustic_description: A harsh far-carrying low- to mid-frequency call with strong noisy energy, typically less sharply high-pitched than the shriek components of choruses.

semantic_description: Used in acute arousal and often embedded in chorus bouts or sudden disturbance contexts.
acoustic_description: A piercing harsh high-frequency call with intense noisy energy and a more sharply cutting quality than the lower roar.

semantic_description: Used in close social interactions and lower-arousal contexts such as within-group coordination or affiliative contact.
acoustic_description: A softer lower-amplitude tonal call with smoother harmonic structure than the loud roaring signals.

semantic_description: Associated with agonistic or defensive interactions at closer range.
acoustic_description: A low rough growling call with noisy spectral structure and variable duration.

semantic_description: Used in routine social coordination and low-intensity interactions among nearby group members.
acoustic_description: A rapid series of brief notes forming a chattering bout that is quieter and more locally directed than the main long-distance calls.

semantic_description: Used in close-range soliciting or dependent-young contexts and other low-distance social interactions.
acoustic_description: A short relatively tonal call with a compact, plaintive contour and less noisy energy than shrieks.

semantic_description: Included as a brief arousal-related call type used to draw attention in local interactions, though context boundaries remain uncertain.
acoustic_description: A short abrupt call with a compact somewhat rough spectrum distinct from tonal hums and extended roars.

semantic_description: Produced during sudden disturbance and sometimes in intergroup communication, especially by adult males in higher-arousal situations.
acoustic_description: A rapid series of two to five short roar-like bursts with harsh noisy structure and abrupt delivery.

semantic_description: Reported mainly from males during the reproductive season and treated here as a mating-related display or advertisement call.
acoustic_description: A moderately loud call with clearer tonal structure than a roar and more sustained harmonic energy than brief chatter-like calls.

semantic_description: Associated with urgency for re-aggregation and often appears at the end of roar-shriek choruses, helping coordinate regrouping under arousal.
acoustic_description: A sustained urgent call rich in harmonic overtones that may sound more tonal or noisy-tonal depending on delivery.

semantic_description: Emitted by males during the breeding season when approaching females to mate and therefore best treated as a courtship or appeasement display.
acoustic_description: A clear-toned call overlaid with some noisy variability, acoustically smoother than a roar but more complex than a plain mew.

semantic_description: Emitted specifically in response to ground or mammalian predators (in contrast to abrupt roars used for aerial predators); functions to alert group members and trigger rapid aggregation in high-arousal antipredator contexts.
acoustic_description: A series of rapid, discrete noisy pulses or squawking bursts with broadband energy, distinct from the more sustained roar-shriek and shorter than the abrupt roar sequence; each pulse is brief with a rough, staccato quality.

semantic_description: Used especially by males in colony display, spacing, and social advertisement.
acoustic_description: A loud explosive bark with abrupt onset and strong broadband energy.

semantic_description: Used in close-range warning and conflict.
acoustic_description: A rough low call with threat-like quality and variable duration.

semantic_description: Used in mother-pup recognition and reunion.
acoustic_description: A higher-pitched call with stronger tonal structure than adult male barks.

semantic_description: Used by adult females during local social and especially mother-pup reunion interactions in dense colonies.
acoustic_description: A shorter, more tonal social call than the main male bark.

semantic_description: Used in high-arousal male display and conflict contexts during territorial or breeding interactions.
acoustic_description: A longer lower-frequency vocalization more sustained than a bark and rougher than mild mother-pup calls.

semantic_description: Used at close range in routine interaction, low-level warning, or mild social negotiation.
acoustic_description: A short, lower-amplitude, low-frequency social sound with less explosive onset than a bark and less duration than a growl.

semantic_description: Produced by pups during acute disturbance, separation, or threat, prompting attention from nearby adults.
acoustic_description: A more urgent and harsher pup vocalization than the ordinary reunion bleat, often emitted as repeated high-pitched bursts.

semantic_description: Produced in aquatic social contexts; documented in underwater vocalization studies alongside barks and click trains, likely functioning in short-range social signalling.
acoustic_description: A rising-falling frequency-modulated tonal call produced underwater, resembling a brief whinny with rapid pitch excursion.

semantic_description: Part of a graded female threat-vocal sequence progressing from bark through squeal to belch and growl; emitted during escalated aggressive interactions in the colony.
acoustic_description: A sharp, high-pitched squealing burst with noisy broadband energy, more intense than a bark but shorter than a sustained growl.

semantic_description: Main adult male advertisement used in territory defense and mate attraction, with socially learned local dialect structure.
acoustic_description: A stereotyped whistle-and-trill song with distinct introductory phrases and terminal trilled or buzz-like components, varying among dialect populations.

semantic_description: Helps maintain flock or pair coordination during movement and short-distance displacement.
acoustic_description: Brief, high-pitched, simple notes given in flight or at takeoff, much shorter and less elaborate than full song.

semantic_description: Used in everyday social interactions, local spacing, and close-range cohesion.
acoustic_description: Short, simple chip notes exchanged at close range, less intense than alarm calls and less prolonged than song.

semantic_description: Used in alarm and disturbance situations, especially around nests or when predators are nearby.
acoustic_description: Harsher, more buzzing vocalization than simple chips, often produced rapidly in agitated contexts.

semantic_description: Used in routine local communication between nearby individuals.
acoustic_description: A short simple call used in close-range social contexts, less sharp than flight or alarm calls.

semantic_description: Included as a named shared-sex call from the non-song repertoire; available descriptions suggest it often signals imminent locomotion or movement-related social tension.
acoustic_description: A softer modulated call with a whining contour, less abrupt than pink and less harsh than the rasping altercation vocalization.

semantic_description: Used during altercations and other close-range antagonistic encounters.
acoustic_description: A harsh rasping call rougher and noisier than pink or whine calls.

semantic_description: Used by nestlings or fledglings to solicit provisioning and parental care.
acoustic_description: A repeated solicitation call delivered by dependent young.

semantic_description: Produced by juveniles during the sensorimotor phase of song learning; considered practice or babbling-like behavior occurring before plastic song and final crystallized song are established.
acoustic_description: A soft, rambling, variable vocalization resembling an underdeveloped or incomplete form of the adult song; notes are disorganized compared to crystallized song, with variable pitch contours and less precise timing.

semantic_description: Given in response to aerial predators such as hawks; the acoustic structure makes it hard for raptors to locate the caller, functioning as a cryptic alarm signal to other flock or group members.
acoustic_description: A high-pitched, thin, sustained pure tone with a narrow frequency spread, difficult to localize acoustically due to gradual onset and offset and frequency above 7 kHz.
